chapters.summary: Writing from prison, Paul gives thanks for the Philippian believers and encourages them to strive together for the gospel, explaining that for him to live is Christ and to die is gain.
keyPoints: Paul gives thanks for the believers' partnership in advancing the gospel, and is confident that God will complete the good work he has begun in them.
Even in his chains Paul boldly proclaims the gospel, and rejoices that Christ is being preached, whatever the motives of those who preach him.
Paul urges believers to live in a manner worthy of the gospel, standing firm in one spirit and striving together with one mind for the faith of the gospel.
themes: A View of Life, Death, and Unity
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us view our fellow workers with gratitude, confident that God's work in them will surely be accomplished. Let us center our lives on Christ, live in a manner worthy of the gospel, and stand united with the rest of the body.

chapters.summary: Paul urges believers to have the mind of Christ Jesus, to be humble and united, and to hold out the word of life, shining like lights in the world.
keyPoints: United in Christ, believers are exhorted to comfort and encourage one another, to be of one mind, and to avoid selfish ambition and empty conceit.
Though Christ existed in the form of God, he emptied himself and took the form of a servant, becoming obedient even to death on the cross.
Believers are to work out their salvation with fear and trembling, blameless, shining like lights as they hold out the word of life.
chapters.application: In our daily relationships with others, let us gird ourselves with humility, considering others more important than ourselves, and follow Christ's example of self-giving, so that peace and love may fill our homes and our church.

chapters.summary: Paul urges believers to rejoice in the Lord, warns against those who boast in the flesh, and testifies how he counts everything as loss for the sake of Christ, pressing on to gain him.
keyPoints: Paul warns believers to beware of the dogs, the evildoers, and those who mutilate the flesh - true circumcision is worshiping God by the Spirit.
Paul lists his own advantages according to the flesh, yet counts everything as loss for the sake of Christ, treasuring the knowledge of Christ above all things.
Forgetting what lies behind and straining toward what lies ahead, Paul presses on toward the goal to win the prize of God's heavenly calling in Christ Jesus.
chapters.application: Let us lay aside self-righteousness and past achievements, treasure the knowledge of Christ above all things, press forward each day to follow him toward God's goal, and rejoice in the Lord in every circumstance.

chapters.summary: Paul urges believers to rejoice in the Lord, and to experience the peace of God through gentleness, prayer, and dwelling on what is good.
keyPoints: Believers are urged to rejoice in the Lord always, and to let their gentleness be known to everyone.
Believers are taught to bring every need to God through prayer, petition, and thanksgiving.
Believers are encouraged to dwell on what is true, righteous, pure, and admirable, and to follow Paul's example.
chapters.application: When facing anxiety, let us bring everything to God, replacing worry with prayer, experiencing the peace he gives, and cultivating a heart of constant gratitude.
